$comment: Executable names that must NEVER appear in a catalogue entry. Shared by the validator (catalogue/index.ts, which fails the seed) and the generator (tools/build-steam-tier.mjs, which filters them out). See the header comment in catalogue/index.ts for why this is a correctness rule and not tidiness.
reason: The desktop client resolves a catalogue name against every RUNNING process and adds the full path of whatever matched. A name shared with unrelated software therefore routes that unrelated software. The worst case is not a missing game -- it is a customer picking Minecraft and silently putting their employer's Java VPN client on the tunnel.
$note_on_anticheat: battleye.exe and easyanticheat.exe stay denied because no source names either and they were speculative. BEService.exe and BEService_x64.exe came off this list once BattlEye's own FAQ was read directly: they are real, first-party, and used only by games, so they ship in the battleye-anti-cheat row rather than being repeated across every BattlEye title.
